title: Microsoft Purview Data Security Investigations: personal data examination
summary: The briefing passes: the examination workflow, consumption billing, permissions and audit operations are supported by Microsoft documentation, and the release details match the roadmap. A minor clarification should acknowledge inconsistent role-group names across Microsoft's permissions and investigation-access pages.

claims.claim: Personal data examination is a Microsoft Purview Data Security Investigations feature.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Data Security Investigations – Introducing new personal data examination

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: The roadmap target is April CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "April CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The record provides no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: DSI adds an examination focus area for identifying personal data.
claims.quote: Data Security Investigations (DSI) is introducing a new examination focus area concentrated on identifying personal data.

claims.claim: The examination extracts personal data including names and account numbers from selected items.
claims.quote: The personal data examination will identify and extract various types of personal data from the selected items including but not limited to, names, addresses, bank account numbers, and more.

claims.claim: Personal data examination works alongside DSI's other AI-powered analysis capabilities.
claims.quote: This addition works alongside DSI’s AI-powered content analysis features, such as categorization, AI search, and examination for risk, which help surface data security risks buried in data.

claims.claim: DSI is a Microsoft Purview solution for analysing content associated with data security incidents.
claims.quote: Use examination to run deep content analysis with AI on selected data items. This examination helps you find security risks buried within impacted data.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: AI identifies and extracts personal data from selected investigation items.
claims.quote: Personal data: Personal data processing identifies and extracts personal data from selected data items, including names, email addresses, employee IDs, IP addresses, and other PII.

claims.claim: The other examination focus areas include Credentials, Risk, Mitigation and Custom.
claims.quote: You can choose examination processing for the following focus areas: Credentials ... Risks ... Mitigation ... Personal data ... Custom

claims.claim: The examination workflow starts at Data Security Investigations in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Go to Data Security Investigations in the Microsoft Purview portal and sign in by using the credentials for a user account assigned Data Security Investigations permissions.

claims.claim: Select Investigations in the left navigation.
claims.quote: Select Investigations in the left navigation.

claims.claim: Select an investigation and then Analysis.
claims.quote: Select an investigation, and then select Analysis on the navigation bar.

claims.claim: Select one or more items and then Examine.
claims.quote: Select one or more items, and then select Examine on the command bar.

claims.claim: Choose the stated Personal data option in Choose a focus area.
claims.quote: Select Personal data: Identify and extract the personally identifiable information in selected evidence in the Choose a focus area field.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Prerequisites; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Examinations are configured for scoped items after Add to scope completes.
claims.quote: Complete the following steps to identify personal data in items included in the investigation scope: ... Add to scope must complete before you can configure examinations.

claims.claim: Results include High, Medium or Low risk levels for personal data in each item.
claims.quote: Risk level: The risk levels for all personal data found in the item. Values include High, Medium, and Low.

claims.claim: Results indicate whether each item contains personal data.
claims.quote: Contains Personal Data: Indication if the data item contains personal data. Values are Yes or No.

claims.claim: Results list the personal data types found in each item.
claims.quote: Type of Personal Data: A list of personal data types found in the data item.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Results include the extracted personal data values themselves.
claims.quote: Personal Data Found: A list of extracted personal data values from the data item.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Results include surrounding text snippets for the personal data.
claims.quote: Surrounding Snippet: The text or string values surrounding the personal data details. This information helps with determining the context in which the personal data appears in the data item.

claims.claim: Results include the AI's classification reasoning and risk rationale.
claims.quote: Thought Process: A summary of the reasoning as to why the personal data associated with the item was classified and its risk level rationale.

claims.claim: Results include processing errors.
claims.quote: Errors: A summary of any processing errors encountered when the AI process runs.

claims.claim: Microsoft's High examples include SSN/National ID and bank account numbers.
claims.quote: | High | SSN/National ID, bank account numbers, financial account numbers, routing numbers |

claims.claim: Microsoft's Medium examples include email addresses, phone numbers and medical record numbers.
claims.quote: | Medium | Email addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, medical record numbers, insurance IDs |

claims.claim: Microsoft's Low examples include full names and addresses.
claims.quote: | Low | Full names, addresses, device identifiers |

claims.claim: The personal data examples are not a comprehensive list.
claims.quote: These examples aren't a comprehensive list of all personal data types detected by the examination.

claims.claim: Microsoft positions the feature for breach privacy impact assessment and identifying affected individuals.
claims.quote: Data breach privacy impact assessment: Run personal data examinations on impacted files to quickly determine which personal data types were exposed and which individuals might be affected.

claims.claim: Microsoft positions examination findings as support for regulatory notification decisions.
claims.quote: Use the structured examination results, including risk levels, personal data types, and AI-generated reasoning, to support compliance reporting and regulatory notification decisions.

claims.claim: Personal data findings can be reviewed within the DSI investigation workspace.
claims.quote: When the examination process completes for a focus area, select Probing history from the command bar on the right side of the investigation scope page. In the Probing history pane, select View details for a specific examination process.

claims.claim: Investigation membership controls investigation access in addition to DSI role-group permissions.
claims.quote: You can add or remove users to manage who can access the investigation. However, before a user can access an investigation (and perform tasks in the investigation), you must add the user to the Data Security Investigations Manager role group in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.fix: Add this qualification to the existing investigation-access sentence: 'Microsoft's investigation-access page still names a Data Security Investigations Manager role group as a prerequisite, whereas its permissions page lists Admins, Investigators and Reviewers.' Retain the existing citations to https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/data-security-investigations-settings-access-permissions and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/data-security-investigations-permissions.

claims.claim: Data Security Management and Insider Risk Management include the Data Security Investigation Contributor role.
claims.quote: | Data Security Management | Data Security Investigation Contributor | Contributor access | ... | Insider Risk Management | Data Security Investigation Contributor | Contributor access |

claims.claim: The Data Security Investigation Contributor role does not include AI job execution.
claims.quote: This role doesn't include access to data storage, AI job execution, or the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard.

claims.claim: Compliance Administrator and Organization Management include the Data Security Investigation Admin role.
claims.quote: | Compliance Administrator | Data Security Investigation Admin | Full administrative access | ... | Organization Management | Data Security Investigation Admin, Data Security Investigation Contributor | Administrative and contributor access |

claims.claim: Personal data examination does not take effect in tenants that have not set up DSI.
claims.quote: Before you can use Data Security Investigations in your organization, you must configure both billing models.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Personal data examination is user-opt-in within configured DSI: an investigator chooses the focus area and starts a run.
claims.quote: Select Personal data: Identify and extract the personally identifiable information in selected evidence in the Choose a focus area field. ... Select Examine to start the AI analysis.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The feature's licensing model is consumption through DSI storage and AI capacity billing.
claims.quote: Billing in Data Security Investigations is based solely on the combination of the amount of stored data and the associated computing capacity needed for AI analysis. It isn't based on a dedicated enterprise plan or license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence; rationale: cost
claims.claim: DSI charges are not covered by a dedicated enterprise plan or licence, but are based on storage and AI compute usage.
claims.quote: Billing in Data Security Investigations is based solely on the combination of the amount of stored data and the associated computing capacity needed for AI analysis. It isn't based on a dedicated enterprise plan or license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meters
claims.claim: DSI storage is pay-as-you-go per gigabyte per month for data associated with all investigations.
claims.quote: The storage meter for Data Security Investigations uses the pay-as-you-go billing model. You pay for storage on a gigabyte (GB) per month basis for stored data associated with all investigations in your organization.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: AI examination consumes Data Security Investigations Compute Units and is billed pay-as-you-go for the compute units used.
claims.quote: Data Security Investigations uses the pay-as-you-go billing model for AI capacity. You need compute units for deep analysis and AI-related processing in your investigations. You pay only for the compute units you use.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Meters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: DSI pay-as-you-go charges use the Azure subscription and resource group linked during setup.
claims.quote: Azure subscription: The Azure subscription you want to assign to the storage meter. Resource group: The resource group in your Azure subscription you want to assign to the storage meter.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The billing page lists the number of files analysed as a cost variable for examination.
claims.quote: | Examination | Number of files analyzed | ... These variables primarily influence the cost for compute unit billing. They work together to determine the exact amount of compute unit usage per investigation.

claims.claim: Examination can require significant compute units even for smaller amounts of data.
claims.quote: Using examination in Data Security Investigations might require a significant number of compute units, even for smaller amounts of data included in an investigation scope.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spend controls; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Azure budgets at DSI resource-group and meter level.
claims.quote: Create budgets for the Data Security Investigations resource group and meter level.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spend controls; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends spend alerts at thresholds such as 50%, 75% or 90%.
claims.quote: Configure alerts when spending approaches defined thresholds (for example, 50%, 75%, or 90%).

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spend controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends the in-product estimator for planning investigation costs.
claims.quote: Before launching an investigation, use the in-product cost estimator to anticipate costs based on investigation size and the analyses you plan to conduct.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spend controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends monitoring storage and compute spending with the usage dashboard.
claims.quote: Monitor usage with the usage dashboard: Use the usage dashboard to track storage and compute unit spending within Data Security Investigations in real time.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spend controls; controls[3].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Azure budgets alert on thresholds but do not stop consumption or jobs.
claims.quote: Notifications are triggered when the budget thresholds are exceeded. Resources aren't affected, and your consumption isn't stopped.

claims.where: Scope: Processing location; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: AI processing can be configured for Australia/New Zealand, Europe, United Kingdom or United States.
claims.quote: You can choose where to use compute units from any of the following locations: Australia/New Zealand (ANZ); Europe (EU); United Kingdom (UK); United States (US).

claims.where: Scope: Processing location; Risk assessment: Data exposure

claims.quote: You can opt in to having compute units provisioned and AI analysis processing done anywhere in the world to mitigate potential disruptions in case your primary location experiences high activity.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends AI processing anywhere with available GPU capacity.
claims.quote: Microsoft recommends having compute units and AI processing done anywhere with available GPU capacity.

claims.quote: Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page, then select Role groups in the left navigation. ... Select one of the Data Security Investigations role groups, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to a role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: Role-group permissions can take up to 30 minutes to apply.
claims.quote: After you configure your role groups, it might take up to 30 minutes for the role group permissions to apply to assigned users across your organization.
